transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, doctor, mostly it’s my sleep. I don’t sleep right anymore. I’ll lie there a long time trying to drift off, and then if I do sleep, I wake up from bad dreams or even just little noises. After that I can’t seem to settle back down. I don’t want to make too much of it, but it’s been bothering me enough I thought I ought to ask about it.
Have you been feeling more stressed or anxious than usual lately?

A little more, I suppose. I try not to make a fuss about it, but when I go somewhere now, I find myself looking around first—like what might fall, where the exits are, whether the floor or steps look steady—before I can really sit easy. I don’t know if that counts as anxious, but it’s something I’ve been doing.
Do you find yourself worrying about things more often than you used to?

Yes… I suppose I do, more than I used to. I don’t mean to sound silly, doctor, but I catch myself thinking ordinary things aren’t as safe as they ought to be. Like if I just trust something simple, it might turn on me somehow. I know that probably doesn’t make much sense.
Are there any places or situations you've been avoiding lately?

Well… maybe a little, yes. I don’t know if I’d call it avoiding exactly, but I do find reasons not to go over to the senior center much. And at home, I’ve been putting off things in the garage, especially around the tools… and that spot where I used to keep the ladder. I suppose I steer clear of it more than I let on.
Do you ever find yourself reliving a frightening or unpleasant experience from the past?

Sometimes, yes… not all the time, but it happens. Like if I hear metal scrape, or I see a ladder leaning in somebody’s yard, it sort of jumps right back into my head before I can stop it. For a moment it feels like I’m under there again, waiting for help. I don’t mean to make it sound worse than it is, doctor, but… that does happen.
Did something specific and frightening happen to you in the past that involves a ladder?

Yes… it did, doctor. I don’t like making too much of it, but something happened with a ladder, and now sometimes if I hear metal scrape or see one leaning in somebody’s yard, it all comes back real sudden. For a moment it’s like I’m under there again, just waiting for somebody to help me. Does that make sense?
Do you find yourself trying to avoid thinking about or remembering what happened with the ladder?

Yes… I suppose I do, though I don’t always call it that. I try to keep busy or put it out of my mind, and I keep finding reasons not to go over to the senior center much. At home, I avoid working around the garage too, especially near the tools and the place where I used to keep that ladder. I know that probably sounds a bit silly, but… that’s what I’ve been doing.
{"intent": "determine the presence of hyperarousal symptoms", "question": "Do you often feel "on edge" or have difficulty relaxing?"}

Yes, I guess I do a little. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m jumpy all day, but when I go somewhere now, I catch myself looking around first… like what could fall, where the exits are, whether the floor or the steps seem steady. Once I’ve checked things over, then I can sit easier. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you stopped doing any activities that you used to enjoy because of your fears or worries?

Yes… I have, a bit. I keep telling myself I’m just busy, but I do find reasons not to go to the senior center like I used to. And I don’t much like working around the garage anymore, especially near the tools or where I kept that ladder. I know it may not sound like much, but I guess I’ve been avoiding those things.
Do you try to push away or avoid thoughts and memories related to the ladder accident?

Yes… I do, though I try not to make too much of it. I’ll tell myself I’m just busy, but I keep finding reasons not to go over to the senior center, and I don’t really like working around the garage anymore—especially near the tools or that spot where I used to keep the ladder. I suppose that’s me avoiding it, isn’t it?
How much of your daily life would you say is affected by the things you're avoiding?

Well… I still get through my regular day, you know. I wash up, eat, do the basic things. So I don’t want to make it sound like I can’t function.

But I suppose it has changed things more than I like to admit. I don’t go to the senior center much now, and around the house I avoid certain chores enough that my wife ends up doing things I used to handle. And I haven’t been seeing my bridge friends much either. So… my days are a bit smaller now, I guess. Is that what you mean?
Would you say that avoiding these places and activities is causing significant distress or problems in your relationships?

I wouldn’t want to say it’s a big problem… I mean, my wife and I are all right. But yes, I suppose it causes some strain. She’s had to take over chores I used to do, because I keep finding reasons not to go near certain things around the house.

And I don’t get out to the senior center much, or see my bridge friends like before. So I guess it’s not ruining everything, but it has made my world smaller. That counts as a problem, doesn’t it?
How long have you been experiencing these sleep disturbances and anxiety symptoms?

It’s been… well, pretty much since the ladder accident. That was about a year and seven months ago now. I guess I kept thinking it would settle down on its own, but it’s been hanging around since then.
Would you say that avoiding these places and activities is something you feel like you're unable to control?

I don’t know if I’d say I’m unable to control it exactly… that sounds a little strong. But I do keep catching myself making excuses.

Like with the senior center, I’ll tell myself I’m tired or maybe next week. And around the garage, I’ll find some other little job to do instead, especially if it means going near the tools or that spot where I used to keep the ladder. So… I guess I’m not choosing it as freely as I’d like to think.
Would you say that your avoidance of certain places and activities is interfering with your daily life most of the time?

Most of the time might be putting it a little strong… I still get through my basic routines, you know, meals and getting dressed and things like that.

But yes, I suppose it does interfere more than I like to admit. I don’t go to the senior center much anymore, and I’ve stopped seeing my bridge friends the way I used to. Around the house I avoid enough that my wife ends up doing chores I used to handle. So my days are… smaller, I guess. If that makes sense.
Would you say that your avoidance of certain places and activities is something that you think about every day?

I wouldn’t say I sit and think about it every minute, no… but yes, in some way it does come up most days.

I’ll think, “Maybe I should go by the senior center,” and then I find a reason not to. Or I’ll see something that needs doing in the garage and, well, if it’s near the tools or that place where I kept the ladder, I sort of steer myself away from it. I don’t know if that’s the right way to put it, but it’s there in the back of my mind pretty often.
